standard.title: Reaction Types and Reaction Rates
standard.description: identify patterns in synthesis, decomposition and displacement reactions and investigate the factors that affect reaction rates
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can write balanced chemical equations and apply conservation of mass (AC9S9U07). They can identify physical and chemical changes (AC9S8U07). They have not yet classified reactions by type (synthesis, decomposition, displacement) or investigated reaction rate factors quantitatively.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students define and represent synthesis, decomposition and displacement reaction types, identify patterns across reaction examples, predict products from reaction type, and investigate how temperature, concentration, surface area and catalysts affect reaction rates.

nodes.label: Reaction types show patterns in how reactants become products
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can define synthesis, decomposition and displacement reactions, represent each using balanced equations, and identify the reaction type from a given equation or description.
nodes.minimum_width: Students define synthesis, decomposition and displacement reactions and write or identify a balanced equation for each type.
nodes.typical_width: Students define and represent all three reaction types using molecular models, word equations and balanced symbolic equations; identify reaction type from given equations; predict products from reaction type; and examine examples of each type in familiar contexts (metal oxidation, acid-metal reactions, decomposition in extracting metals).
wider: Investigate chemical reactions employed by First Nations Australians in producing substances such as acids and ethanol — examining traditional chemical knowledge as applied chemistry
Investigate methods First Nations Australians use to convert toxic plants into edible food products — examining the chemistry underlying traditional food processing
Examine reactions used to produce a range of useful products — connecting reaction type knowledge to industrial chemistry applications

response_modes.reason: First Nations chemical knowledge in food processing and substance production places reaction type classification in a culturally and chemically rich context. Width investment at this node extends the range of reaction contexts examined rather than adding depth-on-fewer-phenomena.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations chemical knowledge in food processing and substance production provides sophisticated and culturally significant applications of reaction chemistry. These are elaboration-grounded directions with genuine chemical depth.
success_criteria: Defines synthesis, decomposition and displacement reactions
Writes or identifies a balanced equation for each reaction type
Predicts products for a given reaction type

nodes.label: Reaction rate is affected by multiple factors
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how temperature, concentration, surface area and catalysts affect reaction rate, and investigate at least one factor quantitatively.
nodes.minimum_width: Students explain how at least three factors affect reaction rate with a particle-level explanation for each.
nodes.typical_width: Students explain the particle-level mechanism by which temperature (particle energy and collision frequency), concentration (particle density and collision frequency), surface area (exposed particles) and catalysts (alternative lower-energy pathway) each affect reaction rate; design and conduct fair test investigations of at least one factor; and represent rate data graphically.
wider: Investigate the effect of a range of factors — temperature, concentration, surface area and catalysts — on reaction rates, designing fair tests for each

Predict how green chemistry principles (minimising waste, reducing energy, using environmentally friendly processes) will affect industrial chemistry — connecting rate and reaction type knowledge to sustainability
Examine reactions used to extract metals and identify the reaction type and rate considerations involved

response_modes.reason: Students commonly understand temperature as a rate factor without being able to explain why at a particle level, and miss how surface area and catalysts operate. Encountering rate factor explanations across all four factors — with particle-level reasoning for each — builds a more complete and mechanistically grounded understanding.

success_criteria: Explains how at least three factors affect reaction rate with particle-level reasoning
Investigates at least one factor and represents rate data graphically
